title: So Did the Hebrew Prophet Raise
description: So Did the Hebrew Prophet Raise in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 112, headed “The brazen serpent; or, Looking to Jesus, John 3. 14 15 16”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: So did the He-brew pro-phet raise The bra-zen ser-pent high, The woun-ded felt im-me-diate ease, The camp for-bore to die.

lines: So did the Hebrew prophet raise
But Christ performs a nobler cure,
When Faith lifts up her eyes.
High on the cross the Saviour hung,
High in the heavens he reigns:
Here sinners by th' old serpent stung
When God's own Son is lifted up,
The Jew beholds the glorious hope,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
